items.title: Qualifier intro buries the fighters under stacked UI
items.what: On the QUALIFIER vs HasanAbi pre-fight screen, ROUND 1/5 pill, giant QUALIFIER title, vs line, flavor-text bar, gold FIGHT button, and STARTING IN n countdown all stack over the upper/mid frame while the two fighters are pushed into the lower third with their feet cropped by the stance/technique sticks.
items.why: First-time players cannot read body language or spacing before the bout; the cinematic dojo and character art—the game's hook—are hidden behind chrome in the most important 5 seconds.
items.how: Collapse to one top pill (ROUND 1/5 · QUALIFIER), one centered title block that fades on FIGHT, and move the flavor line into a single thin subtitle. Raise the fighter root so stances sit fully above the stick bank; hide sticks until the countdown reaches 1.

items.title: Stance/Technique sticks show conflicting legends
items.what: During live bouts a semi-transparent bar directly above the twin sticks lists '◄ step ▲ jump ► step ▼ crouch' and '◄ back ► forward ▲ up ▼ down', while the sticks themselves already have arrow glyphs on the rings. The bar collides with the fighters' feet and duplicates the same information.
items.why: On a 390px-wide phone the extra bar steals vertical space from the 3D stage, creates visual noise under the characters, and teaches nothing the glyphs don't already teach—hurting readability mid-combo.
items.how: Delete the floating STANCE/TECHNIQUE text bar entirely. Keep only the ring arrow glyphs; on first run show a one-time 2-second coach mark that calls out 'Left stick = stance · Right stick = technique' then never repeat.

items.title: IPPON / WAZA-ARI banners obscure the scoring hit
items.what: When a point lands (Spinning Back Kick IPPON, Stepping Lunge Punch IPPON, Lunge Punch WAZA-ARI) a massive centered title card covers the exact moment of contact and both fighters' torsos for over a second while the scoreboard only ticks after the banner.
items.why: Point karate is about seeing the clean hit. Covering the contact frame removes the satisfaction and the learning signal of why the point was awarded—especially punishing on half-point vs full-point distinctions.
items.how: Shrink the announcement to a top-third lockup (scoreboard-adjacent) that doesn't cover the fighters; trigger a 6–8 frame freeze on the contact pose plus a brief limb highlight; let the full-screen card appear only for match-point or bout-win.

items.title: Twin sticks sit on the bottom edge with no safe-area padding
items.what: In every in-fight screenshot the STANCE and TECHNIQUE dual-zone sticks are flush with the physical bottom of the 390×844 frame; the home-indicator / gesture zone overlaps the lower arrow segments and the stick labels.
items.why: Players will fat-finger stance changes or accidentally swipe-to-home mid-exchange. Unreliable input is the fastest way to quit a twin-stick fighter.
items.how: Add a permanent bottom safe-area inset (≥34px) and lift the entire stick bank above it. Increase the active knob hit diameter to ≥56px and keep a dead-zone gutter between the two sticks so thumbs don't cross-talk.

items.title: Win/loss results feel static and slow to rematch
items.what: HASANABI WINS / ASMONGOLD WINS screens show a single frozen kick pose, large score, and a REMATCH button with an 8-second 'STARTING IN' timer; the defeated fighter just stands in the last frame with no reaction or camera change.
items.why: After a tense point bout the celebration/defeat beat is the emotional payoff. A static pose plus forced 8s wait makes victories feel hollow and losses feel like a UI stall, killing the 'one more run' impulse.
items.how: Play a short win/lose camera push and a one-time fighter reaction (arms-up or knee-drop). Make REMATCH immediately tappable; drop the auto-start countdown to 3s or replace it with a silent fill bar so players who want to queue can skip.
